title: CARDIO-TTRansform: A Study to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of Eplontersen (Formerly Known as ION-682884, IONIS-TTR-LRx and AKCEA-TTR-LRx) in Participants With Transthyretin-Mediated Amyloid Cardiomyopathy (ATTR CM)
off: A Phase 3 Global, Double-Blind, Randomized, Placebo-Controlled Study to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of ION-682884 in Patients With Transthyretin-Mediated Amyloid Cardiomyopathy (ATTR CM)

frSites.f: Centre Hospitalier Universitaire De Nantes - Hôpital Nord Laennec

summary: To evaluate the efficacy of eplontersen compared to placebo in participants with ATTR-CM receiving available standard of care (SoC).
desc: This is a multicenter, double-blind study in 1438 participants, who will be randomized to receive subcutaneous (SC) injections of either eplontersen or placebo once every 4 weeks. Participants will also receive daily supplemental doses of the recommended daily allowance of vitamin A.
elig:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Females must be non-pregnant and non-lactating, and either surgically sterile or post-menopausal or abstinent. If engaged in sexual relations of child-bearing potential, agree to use 1 highly effective contraceptive method
* Males must be surgically sterile or, abstinent or, if engaged in sexual relations with a woman of child-bearing potential, the participant or the participant's non-pregnant female partner must be using a highly effective contraceptive method
* Amyloid deposits in cardiac or non-cardiac tissue confirmed by Congo Red (or equivalent) staining OR technetium scintigraphy (99mTc -3,3-diphosphono-1,2- propanodicarboxylic acid \[DPD-Tc\], 99m Tc-pyrophosphate \[PYP-Tc\], or 99m Tc-hydroxymethylene-diphosphonate \[HMDP-Tc\]) with Grade 2 or 3 cardiac uptake in the absence of abnormal light chains ratio, centrally confirmed
* End-diastolic interventricular septum thickness of \> 12 millimeters (mm) on Screening echocardiogram
* New York Heart Association (NYHA) class I-III

Exclusion Criteria:

* Acute coronary syndrome, unstable angina, stroke, transient ischemic attack (TIA), coronary revascularization, cardiac device implantation, cardiac valve repair, or major surgery within 3 months of Screening
* Cardiomyopathy not primarily caused by ATTR-CM, for example, cardiomyopathy due to hypertension, valvular heart disease, or ischemic heart disease
* Monoclonal gammopathy of undetermined significance (MGUS) and/or alterations in immunoglobulin free light chain (FLC) ratio unless fat, bone marrow, or heart biopsy confirming the absence of light chain and the presence of TTR protein by mass spectrometry or immunoelectron microscopy. For participants with chronic kidney disease (CKD) and without presence of monoclonal protein in blood and urine, the acceptable FLC ratio is 0.26-2.25. Results different from that may be discussed with local hematologist, Investigator and Medical Monitor if the risks associated with the biopsy outweigh the benefits
* Prior liver or heart transplant, and/or Left Ventricular Assist Device (LVAD) or anticipated liver transplant or LVAD within 1 year after randomization
* Current or previous treatment with Tegsedi™ (inotersen) or Onpattro™ (patisiran) or other oligonucleotide or ribonucleic acid (RNA) therapeutic (including small interfering ribonucleic acid \[siRNA\]; does not apply to COVID-19 mitochondrial \[mRNA\] vaccinations)
* Current treatment with diflunisal, doxycycline, with or without ursodeoxycholic acid, and/or non-dihydropyridine calcium-channel blocker (e.g., verapamil, diltiazem). Participants receiving any of these agents must respect a wash-out period of 14 days before randomization.

arms.d: Eplontersen by subcutaneous injection once every 4 weeks
Eplontersen-matching placebo by subcutaneous injection once every 4 weeks

primary.m: Composite Outcome of Cardiovascular (CV) Mortality and Recurrent CV Clinical Events up to Week 140

abstracts:
Jering KS, Skali H, Claggett B, Prasad N, Chen J, Gonzalez-Lopez E, et al. Effects of Eplontersen on Cardiac Structure and Function in Patients With Transthyretin Amyloidosis With Cardiomyopathy: Insights from the CARDIO-TTRansform Trial. Circulation. 2026. doi: 10.1161/CIRCULATIONAHA.126.083722
BACKGROUND: In CARDIO-TTRansform, the TTR (transthyretin) silencer eplontersen did not significantly reduce the primary end point of cardiovascular death and recurrent cardiovascular events in patients with TTR amyloidosis with cardiomyopathy, although treatment effects varied by baseline TTR stabilizer use. Whether eplontersen favorably affects cardiac structure and function is unknown.
METHODS: CARDIO-TTRansform randomized 1432 patients with TTR amyloidosis with cardiomyopathy to eplontersen (45 mg) subcutaneously every 4 weeks or placebo. Echocardiograms were performed at baseline and weeks 61, 97, and 140. Associations of baseline echocardiographic measures with all-cause mortality and the primary end point were evaluated using Cox and semiparametric proportional rates models. Between-group differences at week 140 were analyzed with mixed models for repeated measures.
RESULTS: Among 1426 participants with baseline echocardiograms (mean age, 76±7 years, 91% men, 85% wild type, 57% receiving stabilizers), baseline measures of left ventricular systolic function (LV ejection fraction, global longitudinal strain, stroke volume, myocardial contraction fraction), diastolic function (E wave deceleration time, septal e', average E/e'), and right ventricular function and hemodynamics were independently associated with all-cause mortality or the primary end point. At week 140 (echocardiograms available in 554 patients in the eplontersen group and 506 in the placebo group), eplontersen attenuated increases in mean LV wall thickness (least-squares mean [LSM] difference, -0.24 mm [95% CI, -0.48 to -0.01]) and declines in LV stroke volume (LSM difference, 1.88 mL [95% CI, 0.07-3.69]), myocardial contraction fraction (LSM difference, 0.88% [95% CI, 0.25-1.57]), average E/e' (LSM difference, -0.71 [95% CI, -1.36 to -0.07]), and right ventricular outflow tract velocity-time integral (LSM difference, 0.42 [95% CI, 0.00-0.85]) versus placebo in the overall cohort. Beneficial effects were driven almost exclusively by patients not receiving stabilizers at baseline. No significant treatment effects were observed in patients receiving stabilizers.
CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with TTR amyloidosis with cardiomyopathy, eplontersen modestly attenuated deterioration in prognostically important measures of LV systolic, diastolic and right ventricular function, primarily among patients not receiving stabilizers at baseline. These findings complement the clinical findings of CARDIO-TTRansform and suggest that TTR silencing may attenuate progression of cardiac dysfunction in TTR amyloidosis with cardiomyopathy.

Fontana M, Ambardekar AV, Cappelli F, Cuddy SAM, Davis MK, Garcia-Pavia P, et al. Baseline characteristics of patients with transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy in the CARDIO-TTRansform trial of eplontersen. Eur J Heart Fail. 2026. doi: 10.1093/ejhf/xuag168
AIMS: Eplontersen is an antisense oligonucleotide that suppresses hepatic production of circulating transthyretin (TTR) by targeting TTR mRNA. We present baseline data from an ongoing trial, CARDIO-TTRansform, evaluating eplontersen in patients with TTR amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM) and compare findings across previous ATTR-CM trials.
METHODS AND RESULTS: We evaluated 1432 patients enrolled in CARDIO-TTRansform from March 2020 to July 2023 who received ≥1 dose of study intervention (eplontersen or placebo) and had ≥1 post-baseline measurement. Mean (standard deviation) age was 76.4 (7.1) years; 9.4% were female; 88.8% were White. A total of 211 (14.7%) patients had hereditary/variant ATTR-CM (ATTRv-CM); Val122Ile (p.Val142Ile) was the most common genotype (n = 130). Patients spanned New York Heart Association functional classes I (n = 192), II (n = 997), and III (n = 243); 62.6% were National Amyloidosis Centre disease stage 1. Median (interquartile range) N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide was 2025 (1296-3465) pg/ml; n = 51 measured >8500 pg/ml. Median (interquartile range) high-sensitivity troponin T was 50 (35-69) pg/ml and mean left ventricular ejection fraction was 55.7% (9.7%). At baseline, 57.2% were on TTR stabilizer; 18.4% were on sodium-glucose co-transporter-2 inhibitors.
CONCLUSION: The baseline characteristics of CARDIO-TTRansform were consistent with previous ATTR-CM trials; however, CARDIO-TTRansform evaluated patients with a wide range of disease severity and receiving the contemporary standard of care for ATTR-CM. Overall, blinded baseline data suggest that CARDIO-TTRansform provides a unique opportunity to determine the clinical benefits of eplontersen in a contemporary setting and in clinically relevant subgroups of patients with ATTR-CM.
TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: NCT04136171.

Gillmore JD, Hamatani Y, Fontana M, Vaduganathan M, Claggett BL, Garcia-Pavia P, et al. Gene Silencer Therapy in Transthyretin Amyloid Cardiomyopathy: A Meta-Analysis of Outcomes Trials. JAMA. 2026. doi: 10.1001/jama.2026.17246
IMPORTANCE: Gene-silencing therapies reduce hepatic transthyretin (TTR) production and have been evaluated in phase 3 trials in TTR amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM). However, differences in trial design and background therapies have limited assessment of the overall treatment effect and its consistency according to baseline TTR stabilizer use.
OBJECTIVE: To assess the effect of TTR gene-silencing therapies in patients with ATTR-CM.
DATA SOURCES AND STUDY SELECTION: PubMed was searched through June 15, 2026, for randomized, placebo-controlled, phase 3 outcome trials of gene-silencing therapies in ATTR-CM.

x.titre: Eplontersen dans la cardiomyopathie amyloïde à transthyrétine
x.question: L'eplontersen réduit-il la mortalité cardiovasculaire et les événements cardiovasculaires récurrents dans la cardiomyopathie amyloïde à transthyrétine ?
x.contexte:
La cardiomyopathie amyloïde à transthyrétine (ATTR-CM), héréditaire ou sauvage, est une cause sous-diagnostiquée d'insuffisance cardiaque à fraction d'éjection préservée. Elle résulte du dépôt de fibrilles de transthyrétine (TTR) dans le myocarde. Le pronostic est sombre, avec une survie médiane de quelques années après le diagnostic.

Le tafamidis, stabilisateur de la TTR, a réduit la mortalité et les hospitalisations dans l'étude ATTR-ACT et constitue la référence. Des approches de silençage visent à réduire la production de TTR à la source.

L'eplontersen est un oligonucléotide antisens ciblant l'ARN messager de la TTR, administré par voie sous-cutanée. Il est déjà évalué dans la polyneuropathie amyloïde héréditaire. CARDIO-TTRansform est un essai de phase 3 promu par Ionis, randomisé en double insu contre placebo, chez 1 438 patients, en plus du traitement de référence, dans 21 pays dont la France. Les patients reçoivent une injection toutes les 4 semaines, avec une supplémentation en vitamine A.
x.interet: C'est l'un des plus grands essais dans l'ATTR-CM. Un bénéfice sur la mortalité et les événements cardiovasculaires ferait de l'eplontersen une option complémentaire ou alternative au tafamidis. Il fournira aussi des données sur l'association au traitement de référence.
x.profil: Des adultes de 18 à 90 ans atteints de cardiomyopathie amyloïde à transthyrétine (ATTR-CM), sous traitement de référence.
inclusion: Dépôts amyloïdes confirmés par coloration rouge Congo ou scintigraphie (captation cardiaque grade 2 ou 3) sans anomalie des chaînes légères, avec confirmation centrale
Épaisseur du septum interventriculaire > 12 mm à l'échocardiographie
Contraception efficace selon le sexe et le statut de fertilité
exclusion: Événement cardiovasculaire ou chirurgie majeurs dans les 3 mois (SCA, AVC, AIT, revascularisation, pose de dispositif)
Cardiomyopathie non principalement due à l'ATTR (hypertension, valvulopathie, ischémique)
MGUS ou ratio des chaînes légères anormal, sauf biopsie confirmant l'absence de chaînes légères
Greffe hépatique ou cardiaque, assistance ventriculaire gauche ou greffe prévue dans l'année
Traitement actuel ou antérieur par inotersen, patisiran ou autre oligonucléotide ou ARNsi
Traitement par diflunisal, doxycycline ± acide ursodésoxycholique ou inhibiteur calcique non dihydropyridinique (sevrage de 14 jours)

bras.traitement: Eplontersen par injection sous-cutanée toutes les 4 semaines, avec vitamine A quotidienne (dose non précisée)
Placebo identique par injection sous-cutanée toutes les 4 semaines, avec vitamine A quotidienne

x.duree: Jusqu'à la semaine 140 pour le critère principal ; durée totale non précisée
x.critere: Critère composite de mortalité cardiovasculaire et d'événements cardiovasculaires cliniques récurrents, de l'inclusion jusqu'à la semaine 140
x.resultats: Selon le résumé publié d'une analyse échocardiographique de CARDIO-TTRansform (1432 patients randomisés ; éplontersen 45 mg sous-cutané toutes les 4 semaines ou placebo), l'éplontersen n'a pas réduit de façon significative le critère principal (décès cardiovasculaires et événements cardiovasculaires récurrents), avec un effet variable selon l'utilisation initiale d'un stabilisateur de la TTR. À la semaine 140 (échocardiogrammes disponibles chez 554 patients sous éplontersen et 506 sous placebo), l'éplontersen atténuait l'augmentation de l'épaisseur pariétale ventriculaire gauche (différence -0,24 mm ; IC 95 % -0,48 à -0,01) et la baisse du volume d'éjection (+1,88 mL ; IC 95 % 0,07-3,69). Il atténuait aussi la baisse de la fraction de contraction myocardique (+0,88 % ; IC 95 % 0,25-1,57), l'élévation du rapport E/e' moyen (-0,71 ; IC 95 % -1,36 à -0,07) et la baisse de l'intégrale temps-vitesse de la voie d'éjection du ventricule droit (+0,42 ; IC 95 % 0,00-0,85). Ces effets étaient portés presque exclusivement par les patients sans stabilisateur à l'inclusion, sans effet significatif chez ceux sous stabilisateur. Les auteurs concluent à une atténuation modeste de la dégradation de la fonction cardiaque, surtout sans stabilisateur.
